text:
To: Warehouse Managers
From: Ludovica Ferrante, Supply Chain Director
Subject: Peak-season staffing

As in previous years, demand will peak between mid-November and the end of December, and I should like to confirm the arrangements for temporary staff. [1] Agencies have been asked to supply workers who can start at short notice and who have completed the mandatory safety induction.

Managers are [2] for estimating their requirements by shift and for submitting them to me by 30 September. [3] the cost of temporary labor has risen, the alternative of understaffing would be far more expensive, since late deliveries incur penalties under most of our contracts. [4] requests received after the deadline, we cannot guarantee that agencies will be able to supply the numbers required.

choices: Last year, a shortage of trained staff in the second week of December led to delays that cost the company a major contract.
Last year, a surplus of trained staff in the second week of December led to savings that won the company a major contract.
This year, a shortage of trained staff in the second week of December will lead to delays that cost the company a major contract.
Last year, a shortage of trained agencies in the second week of December led to delays that cost the company a major staff.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says agencies should supply workers who can start at short notice, which responds to last year's shortage; only the first provides that background.
Managers are 'responsible for' estimating requirements; 'responsive' means reacting quickly, and 'respondent' is a noun.
'Although the cost of temporary labor has risen' concedes a drawback before the main argument.
'In the case of requests received after the deadline' introduces the specific situation; the others have different meanings.

text:
Hotel Review: The Alder House, Edinburgh

The Alder House occupies a restored Georgian townhouse five minutes' walk from the castle. [1] Our room, which overlooked a quiet square, combined period features such as high ceilings and sash windows with a modern bathroom and an excellent bed.

Staff were attentive without being intrusive, and breakfast, which uses produce from local suppliers, was consistently good. [2], prices are high: a double room costs almost double the city average, and the lack of a lift may be [3] for guests with limited mobility. [4] these drawbacks, I would stay again without hesitation.

choices: The conversion has been carried out with evident care, and the character of the original building has largely been preserved.
The conversion has been carried out with evident haste, and the character of the original building has largely been lost.
The building has been converted with evident care, and the character of the original staff has largely been preserved.
The conversion was carried out with evident care, and the character of the original building would have been preserved.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes a room that combines period features with modern comfort, which requires a sentence about careful conversion; only the first fits.
'Admittedly' concedes a drawback before the positive verdict, as 'Prices are high' does.
The lack of a lift may be 'problematic' for guests with limited mobility; the others do not fit.
'Despite these drawbacks' is a preposition followed by a noun phrase and concedes the faults.
